subject: [hw] DEC05 -> IP: exact vcodecd integration for the decoder (dispatch, HELLO, FLUSH/CLOSE, dma_info, tick, exit 70, write-combining)
body:
DONE DEC05 posted (N2TEST DEC05 PASS 1150/1150). The decoder service is a module; vcodecd.c is yours, so here is the whole integration surface (also in gpu/hwcodec/daemon/dec/README.md):

  struct n2vcd_dec_ap_n2ap_cfg acfg = { .vcu = vcu, .hw = vhw, .timeout_ms = hw_timeout_ms,
          .guest_stopped = vcodecd_guest_stopped, .guest_ctx = &g };
  adapter = n2vcd_dec_ap_n2ap_create(&acfg);
  struct n2vcd_dec_service_cfg dcfg = { .send = send_to_client, .dma_info = dma_info_wrapper,
          .ctx = &g, .ap = n2vcd_dec_ap_n2ap_ops(), .ap_ctx = adapter,
          .log = daemon_log, .fatal = fatal_guest_stop, .session_idle_ms = g.session_idle_ms };
  dec = n2vcd_dec_service_create(&dcfg);

Rules:
1. Dispatch before your encoder switch: if (n2vcd_dec_service_owns(buf,n)) { n2vcd_dec_service_handle(dec, from, buf, n); return; }. owns() claims OPEN with encoder==0, DEC_HEADER/DEC_FRAME and ids 20..29.
2. FLUSH and CLOSE are shared v1 ids; they are ours only when h.session == n2vcd_dec_service_session(dec). Add that check before the encoder switch (otherwise a decoder FLUSH hits the encoder path and answers E_SESSION/E_UNSUPPORTED).
3. Close notice: n2vcd_dec_service_client_gone(dec, from) (your loop already sees bytes==0).
4. Every loop iteration (<=1 s): n2vcd_dec_service_tick(dec, now_ms()). It polls the guest-stop callback and drops an idle session with seq-0 E_SESSION, exactly like watchdog_poll().
5. guest_stopped: pass your existing n2vhost_join/n2shim check. The service calls fatal on the first request of a dead guest: it sends E_GUEST to the requester (seq) and seq-0 E_GUEST to the other seen clients, logs one line, then calls .fatal. Make .fatal do what fatal_guest_stop() already does (power off best effort, log pc/reason, _exit(70)). Hardware timeouts (-ETIMEDOUT from the AP) are non-fatal and end only the decoder session.
6. dma_info: wrap n2vcd_srv_dma_info(srv, handle, &pa, &bytes). On the host socket it returns -ENOSYS; the service then accepts pa=0 and my fake AP does not need it. On the phone it is what registers each client handle in n2vc_dma for n2ap_vdec.
7. HELLO_OK: dec_codecs must become 3 (H.264|HEVC) once the decoder is linked; the service handles HELLO only in the standalone test daemon, your HELLO reply stays authoritative in vcodecd.
8. Enable write-combining once after vcu create for the decode path: n2vcu_set_write_combining(vcu, 1) (DEC04: 2116 -> 1033 RWVC_REGS calls per AU; default OFF, explicit enable).
9. Session policy: the service allows one decoder session. Running it together with the encoder session is your call; vpud is a single interpreter, so serialising them is the safe v1.
10. Build: add daemon/dec/n2vcd_dec_service.c + daemon/dec/n2vcd_dec_ap_n2ap.c to the daemon link (the adapter needs ap/n2ap_vdec.c + ap/n2vc_dma.c + the ion publish hook, already in the daemon link for VENC). The service has no other dependency.

My e2e uses your daemon/n2vcd_srv.c unchanged with a test-only main (daemon/dec/test/dec_testd.c); a real dec_testd over SOCK_SEQPACKET exercises open/header/add/input/picture/release/flush/close, daemon kill, idle and exit 70. No phone, nothing published.
